title: FDR and q-values
dek: FDR is an expected fraction of false discoveries among rejections. A q-value is an estimated FDR if you reject at this and all more extreme p-values. Neither is a p-value.
story: Let R be the number of rejections and V the number of false ones. FDR = E[V/R | R>0] P(R>0) (Benjamini–Hochberg’s original form; people often write E[V/R] with 0/0 := 0). You tolerate a fraction of mistakes among the hits, not a probability of any mistake.

BH: sort p_{(1)} ≤ … ≤ p_{(m)}, reject k̂ = max {k : p_{(k)} ≤ (k/m) α}. Under independence (and some positive dependence), this controls FDR at α. It is not Bonferroni. The implied threshold is data-dependent — more rejections licence a looser p-cut.

Storey’s q-value estimates, for each test, the FDR of the rejection set that includes this test and all stronger ones, with a π₀ estimate of the null fraction. A q of 0.06 is not a p of 0.06. Caption it as an FDR estimate.
deep: BH is conservative if many alternatives are true (π₀ < 1); Storey estimates π₀ from the right tail of p-values. In a well-powered RNA-seq contrast, π₀ might be 0.8; in a GWAS of a polygenic trait, most SNPs are near-null and π₀ ≈ 1, so BH and Bonferroni-ish thresholds can sit closer.

Dependence: BH remains valid under PRDS-type positive dependence. Strong clumping (the same isolate driving every gene) can still distort. Cluster the tests scientifically (genes, LD blocks) or use permutation of a structured null.
q-value ≠ posterior probability of H₀. A local FDR / two-group model is closer to that Bayesian object and needs a mixing model for p-values. Do not write “q = 0.01 so P(null)=0.01.”

TB catalogue screens (thousands of variants vs a phenotype): FDR is usually the right contract for hypothesis generation. A drug-licensing claim wants a different error rate and a designed experiment.

formulas.label: BH threshold
formulas.expression: k̂ = max{k : p_{(k)} ≤ (k/m) α},   reject p_{(1)}…p_{(k̂)}
formulas.note: Controls FDR at α under independence / PRDS.

formulas.label: q-value (Storey sketch)
formulas.note: Estimated FDR of the rejection set with cutoff p_{(k)}. Monotone-adjusted in software.

visual.caption: From a pile of p-values to a rejection set with an FDR contract: sort, compare to the (k/m)α line, optionally estimate π₀, report q-values. The exit to FWER is Bonferroni/Holm — a different product.

example.title: BH on 10 p-values

steps.title: Compare
steps.body: k=1: 0.001≤0.005 yes. k=2: 0.008≤0.010 yes. k=3: 0.012≤0.015 yes. k=4: 0.020≤0.020 yes. k=5: 0.040>0.025 no. Max k with all the rule (BH takes the largest k that satisfies, including earlier yeses) is k=4.

steps.title: Caption
steps.body: Four discoveries at FDR 5% (BH). Not four p-values < 0.05, and not FWER 5%.

example.takeaway: BH is a comparison to a sloped line, not to 0.05. q-values summarise that line.
